rationale: Genuine no-spec round (no acceptance ArtifactRef dispatched) caps confidence at low, but the diff itself ships a committed story.md whose live Acceptance Criteria directly contradict the shipped design (CR-001, decision_needed) alongside 6 patchable defects (icon swap, re-entrant clone click, two silent-failure edge cases, a request-staleness race, and an untested authorization gate) and 1 standards-blocking commit-format violation (CR-008). 1 finding deferred as pre-existing shared toast logic; 4 findings dismissed as noise (speculative fire-and-forget concern, an untyped-field nitpick, and two theoretical state-desync scenarios that React 18's state-update batching rules out).

standards_review.notes: 28/29 subjects match EPMCDME-XXXX format; 'mcp-clone-flow-ux: add planning artifacts' has no ticket prefix and starts lowercase
no code-quality guide present and no code_quality ArtifactRef was passed
no dangerouslySetInnerHTML/innerHTML, unsafe navigation, env reads, or nosonar additions in changed files

findings.title: Implementation contradicts committed clone-flow spec
findings.problem: The committed story.md's live Acceptance Criteria mandate a non-editable confirmation popup (no MCPServerModal clone mode, no pre-filled draft, clone.svg icon, no-body clone call) and explicitly list the shipped design -- an editable pre-filled MCPServerModal Clone mode, a new suggested-clone-name GET endpoint, and a body-carrying clone POST -- under 'Superseded Criteria — do not implement.'
findings.impact: Either the design doc is stale or the implementation shipped the wrong UX/contract; anyone reviewing against story.md as the spec of record would be approving a change that contradicts its own accompanying documentation, and the actual backend contract (body vs. no-body clone call) is left unverified against any committed source.
findings.recommendation: A human must reconcile the two: either update story.md's Acceptance/Superseded Criteria to reflect the MCPServerModal Clone-mode design actually implemented, or rework the implementation to match the committed confirmation-popup design.

findings.title: Clone/Copy ID icons inverted vs. spec
findings.problem: The 'Clone' menu entry keeps the old CopySvg (copy.svg) icon while the renamed 'Copy ID' entry gets the new ClipboardSvg (clipboard.svg); no clone.svg asset was added at all.
findings.impact: This is the inverse of the documented intent to visually distinguish 'Clone' from 'Copy ID', leaving the two actions' icons confused for users.
findings.recommendation: Assign a dedicated/distinct icon to 'Clone' and keep copy.svg/clipboard.svg consistently on 'Copy ID'.

findings.title: Clone menu item stays clickable while its own modal is open
findings.problem: `disabled={cloningNameFetchPending}` only covers the name-fetch phase; once the Clone modal is open (or submitting), the menu item is clickable again because fetchingCloneNameId has already been cleared in the `finally` block.
findings.impact: A second click on the same row's Clone action re-triggers the name fetch and resets the already-open draft via the mode/cloneSource/suggestedName effect, discarding in-progress edits.
findings.recommendation: Disable or hide the Clone menu item while the Clone modal is open for this row, not only during the name-fetch phase.

findings.title: Empty suggested name isn't treated as 'no suggestion'
findings.problem: `name: suggestedName ?? cloneSource.name` only falls back on null/undefined; an empty-string `suggested_name` from the new backend endpoint passes through unchanged.
findings.impact: If the suggested-clone-name endpoint ever returns an empty string, the Name field opens blank instead of pre-filled with the source name, contradicting the 'server-suggested editable name' requirement.
findings.recommendation: Use an explicit emptiness check (e.g. `suggestedName || cloneSource.name` guarded for undefined, or a trim check) instead of `??`.

findings.title: Save failure can fail completely silently
findings.problem: The catch block dropped its former console.error and now only calls `toaster.error(message)`; `toaster.error` no-ops on a falsy/empty string (`if (!text) return` in utils/toaster.ts), and `??` doesn't fall back on an explicit empty-string backend message.
findings.impact: A backend error response with an empty-string `message` produces zero toast and zero console diagnostics -- a failed save looks like nothing happened, matching Edit's required error UX in spirit but not in this specific edge case.
findings.recommendation: Guard with `||` instead of `??` for the message fallback, and restore a console.error(error) call so a failure is never fully silent.

findings.title: No staleness guard on the suggested-clone-name fetch
findings.problem: `handleCloneMenuClick` has no per-request token/abort guard; `handleAddMCPServer`/`handleEditServer` are not blocked while another row's name fetch is in flight.
findings.impact: Clicking Clone on a second row before the first row's fetch resolves lets whichever resolves last silently overwrite the shared cloneSource/modalMode state, and opening Add/Edit while a clone fetch is still pending can be overwritten into Clone mode on later resolution, discarding in-progress form input.
findings.recommendation: Track the in-flight request per click (a ref/token compared on resolution, or AbortController) and ignore a stale resolution before updating cloneSource/modalMode/showModal.

findings.title: Clone authorization gate has no real test coverage
findings.problem: `canClone = isAdmin || isMaintainer` is computed at MCPManagementPage.tsx:72-74, but every existing test (MCPServerActions.accessibility.test.tsx, MCPServerActions.clone.test.tsx) injects `canClone` as a hardcoded boolean prop directly into MCPServerActions; none renders MCPManagementPage or otherwise exercises the real expression.
findings.impact: An inverted or mistyped operator in the authorization gate (e.g. `&&` instead of `||`, or a dropped `?? false`) would silently ship Clone visibility wrong for maintainers or ordinary viewers, and no existing test would catch it.
findings.recommendation: Add a test that renders MCPManagementPage (or isolates the canClone expression) against admin/maintainer/neither userStore states.

findings.title: Commit subject violates enforced ticket-format regex
findings.problem: Commit subject 'mcp-clone-flow-ux: add planning artifacts' has no EPMCDME ticket prefix and starts lowercase, violating git-workflow.md's enforced regex.
findings.impact: The documented format is enforced by Tekton CI, which blocks on violations.
findings.recommendation: Reword the subject to 'EPMCDME-15538: Add planning artifacts' (or squash it into an adjacent EPMCDME-15538 commit) before the branch is merged.
